rules.Error to avoid: Do not rely on a narrow case list or outdated sources where current scholarship or later authority is material.
rules.Positive target: Use the latest relevant primary authorities and a sufficiently broad range of approved scholarship; identify which sources are central and which are peripheral.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not present a disputed proposition as settled or omit a material opposing view.
rules.Positive target: Identify the strongest contrary judicial or scholarly view, explain its basis, and give a reasoned position.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not treat dissent, obiter, a pending appeal or a secondary source as binding law.
rules.Positive target: State the legal role and hierarchy of material authorities, including majority/dissent and ratio/obiter where relevant.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not cite an entire judgment/article when the relied-on passage can be pinpointed.
rules.Positive target: Provide paragraph or page pinpoints for every material proposition where the source permits them.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not state doctrine or policy effects without explaining their significance to the precise question.
rules.Positive target: Explain why the rule or policy exists and the practical/legal implications of adopting each interpretation.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not create a broad sequence of short, compressed sections that merely touch many topics.
rules.Positive target: Justify the chosen scope, group related issues, and develop fewer material points in sufficient depth with balanced sections.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not use a convenient label where it changes the legal or scientific category.
rules.Positive target: Use the correct legal, scientific and factual terminology and distinguish adjacent concepts before applying them.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not cite one familiar section while omitting a provision or exception that changes the outcome.
rules.Positive target: Identify the governing provision together with material definitions, exceptions, companion sections, commencement and remedies.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not cite a source merely because it supports the thesis without assessing its authority or evidential limits.
rules.Positive target: Evaluate the reliability, status, date and limits of material sources, especially factual, technical and economic claims.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not present unexplained figures or leave obvious arithmetic errors uncorrected.
rules.Positive target: Show the legal basis and workings for material calculations and run an arithmetic consistency check.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not let repeated bullet lists, formulaic mini-conclusions or outline-style prose replace developed analysis.
rules.Positive target: Use sustained academic prose, purposeful headings, transitions and editorially varied conclusions.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not spend most of the answer describing background and postpone engagement with the proposition until the final pages.
rules.Positive target: Integrate evaluation and authority throughout each section.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not rely on vague case names, unsupported abbreviations or an unpinpointed source for a contested proposition.
rules.Positive target: State the exact provision, paragraph, legal role and relevance of each material authority.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not rely almost entirely on cases/statutes for an essay requiring scholarly debate.
rules.Positive target: Use and synthesise approved secondary sources where the task calls for academic evaluation.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not spend material words on remote or excluded topics while a central issue remains underdeveloped.
rules.Positive target: Keep the answer within the set issue and examinable scope while explaining any necessary boundary choice.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not list both outcomes without ranking them or explaining why uncertainty remains.
rules.Positive target: Give a clear but appropriately qualified conclusion and identify the fact that would change it.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not copy a pinpoint or proposition from a secondary source without checking the primary text.
rules.Positive target: Verify the primary source behind any pinpoint borrowed from commentary.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not analyse the wrong offence/claim or import an excluded doctrine because it appears factually adjacent.
rules.Positive target: Classify the correct claim, offence, defence or statutory route before applying its elements.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not omit a central case/provision while discussing peripheral material.
rules.Positive target: Identify and apply the authority or statutory provision that directly controls the issue.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not submit an outline or briefing-note sequence in place of sustained academic analysis.
rules.Positive target: Convert lists and very short sections into connected analytical paragraphs unless a list is functionally necessary.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not lose marks through missing pinpoints, inconsistent citations, bibliography defects or avoidable SPaG errors.
rules.Positive target: Complete a final OSCOLA/SPaG check against the current official guide and institutional checklist.

rules.Error to avoid: Do not allow an obvious arithmetic error or unstated assumption to drive the legal conclusion.
rules.Positive target: Cross-check inputs, dates and arithmetic against the legal assumptions stated.
